summary: The fact layer was cut at 2026-10-22T10:37:01Z, and the pre-market view is built session by session: the US leg is the 2026-10-21 settled close, the A-share and Japan/Hong Kong/Taiwan/Korea legs are the 2026-10-22 close, and crypto is a 24-hour reading. The composite score is 60.03, up 1.57 from 58.46 on the previous session, crossing the 60 threshold into high_risk. Almost the entire increase comes from cross-asset confirmation, which rose from 50 to 62.5 and contributed 1.875 points at a 15 percent weight, because bitcoin's 24-hour return turned negative, down 1.50661 percent, lifting the triggered count from 4 to 5 of 8 signals. The offsetting force is equally clear: the volatility dimension fell to 29.98 as VIX eased from 18.44 to 17.31, removing 0.672 points. US equities closed higher overnight, with NVDA up 2.5408 percent and AMD up 3.3624 percent, while Asia turned weaker today: the two Korean memory names fell 5.487 percent and 4.027 percent, 3 of 11 A-share names rose against 8 decliners, and Nasdaq futures are down 1.8 percent pre-market. The pre-market tone: AI hardware and compute remain elevated, but cracks in cross-asset confirmation and the Asian memory chain are widening together, and whether the 60 band holds depends on the US 10-year at 5.12 percent and the real rate at 2.77 percent.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Cross-asset confirmation at 62.5, with 5 of 8 scored signals triggered, is the single largest contributor at 9.375 points and is also the source of today's 1.57-point increase; it is booked at a 0.8 discount and remains the highest-leverage risk amplifier.
High-yield OAS at 3.33 percent, from 3.29 percent, contributes 6.5632 points; the spread is widening at the margin but sits below the 4 percent trigger, so credit has not confirmed the equity bid.
The 10-year real rate at 2.77 percent, from 2.8 percent, contributes 4.936 points and is the heaviest single macro drag, a standing constraint on long-duration growth valuations.

The 10-year nominal yield is 5.12 percent, from 5.15 percent, with a 10-year minus 2-year spread of 0.33 percentage points, contributing 4.8795 points; a flat curve on top of a high real rate is the defining macro combination.

Share of constituents above the 200-day average is 44.52 percent (69 of 155), contributing 4.1525 points; more than half the market sits below its average, so index strength rests on a narrow set of names.

supporting_signals.claim: Bitcoin is down 1.50661 percent over 24 hours to 82021 dollars with dominance at 60.01 percent, which flipped the bitcoin_down signal into trigger and is the only newly triggered leg taking the cross-asset count from 4 to 5.
Small-cap relative performance is -10.0734 percentage points, with IWM persistently lagging SPY; risk appetite has not broadened beyond the index.
Semis relative performance is -12.1452 percentage points; SOXX weakness against the benchmark points the same way as today's A-share semiconductor decline.
The dollar index is 121.405, from 121.569, still above the 105 trigger line and a weight on emerging markets and commodities.
The 52-week new-low ratio at 5.77 percent (9 names) has edged above the new-high ratio at 5.13 percent (8 names), the weakest cell inside breadth.

contradicting_signals.claim: VIX at 17.31, well below the prior 18.44, pushed the volatility dimension down to 29.98 from 34.46 and removed 0.672 points on its own; on volatility alone, risk is falling.

spy_down did not trigger: US equities closed higher on 2026-10-21, with NVDA up 2.5408 percent, AMD up 3.3624 percent and TSLA up 3.4144 percent; AI hardware and autos were the strongest blocks overnight.
Gold also fell 1.0241 percent, leaving gold_up untriggered, so 2 of 8 signals point the benign way; cross-asset is 5 against 3, not one-sided.

The regime remains risk_on on low volatility or strong momentum; that does not contradict the high_risk score, because the score is lifted by the cross-asset gate while the regime is judged on volatility and momentum, and the 0.91 confidence carries that divergence into the conclusion as it stands.

what_changed_today: The composite rose from 58.46 to 60.03, up 1.57, crossing the 60 threshold into high_risk, the first band change since 2026-10-21.
Cross-asset confirmation rose from 50 to 62.5, a dimension gain of 12.5 points, worth 1.875 points at the 15 percent weight, with bitcoin_down the newly triggered leg.
The volatility dimension fell from 34.46 to 29.98, down 4.48 dimension points, worth -0.672 points and pulling against cross-asset.
The other three dimensions edged higher: macro 73.52 to 74.31, liquidity and credit 70.33 to 70.93, equity structure 63.66 to 64.11, together worth 0.368 points; trend was flat at 42.92.
The A-share close on 2026-10-22 was 3 up against 8 down, a mean decline of 1.52 percent, led lower by the semiconductor and memory chain (603986 down 3.9129 percent, 688825 down 3.0998 percent).
watch_next: Direction at the US open: Nasdaq futures are down 1.8 percent pre-market; if the gap is bought, the cross-asset count holds at 5 of 8 and the score chops around 60, while a widening decline would add spy_down to the trigger set.
FOMC on 2026-10-28 alongside GOOGL and MSFT results, then AMZN on 2026-10-29: repricing risk in a dense event window is concentrated in mega-cap technology.

Treasuries: the 10-year at 5.12 percent is only 0.03 points below its prior level, with the real rate at 2.77 percent; at least one sell-side view expects a breakout around the Fed meeting, which would lift both the macro and cross-asset dimensions.
Whether the Korean memory names, down 5.487 percent and 4.027 percent, transmit to US memory: MU rose 1.9641 percent overnight and is the most direct read on that link.

Optical modules and CPO keep sliding in A-shares, with firms including Eoptolink and Yuanjie responding today that operations and deliveries are normal; further contagion would extend semiconductor weakness from memory into compute interconnect.

bull_case.title: Bull case: volatility keeps easing and cross-asset gives back
points: VIX keeps falling from 17.31, holding the volatility dimension near 29.98, a steady negative contribution on its own.
If the US open absorbs the futures decline, spy_down stays untriggered, cross-asset falls back to 50 and the score retreats to the 58 band.
A 10-year yield back below 5.15 percent would let both the real and nominal legs give way together.

base_case.title: Base case: choppy at the top, hovering at the 60 band
points: Small gains across five dimensions net against the volatility decline, leaving the score chopping between 59 and 62 and the band flipping at the edge of high_risk.
Cross-asset holds at 5 of 8, adding no new trigger and giving back none.
High-yield OAS stays flat near 3.33 percent, short of the 4 percent trigger, so hy_oas_widening remains untriggered.

bear_case.title: Bear case: geopolitics and oil lift inflation expectations and real rates step higher
points: If high-yield OAS breaks 4 percent, or small-cap underperformance widens further, the cross-asset count would rise to 7 and lift the score into the 70 band.
Escalation in the Middle East, with reported talk of a new US-Israeli strike and an intraday oil spike, would push inflation expectations and real rates up together if it feeds through.
If the A-share semiconductor and optical-module decline transmits to US equities, the semis_relative lag already at 12.1452 percentage points would deteriorate further.
